neighbours.label: a preposition or connective linking a person's activity to an institution or place in development or public-health reporting ('training in high school', 'treatment from distant clinics', 'returning home from the bar'), against the same reports without that link
fire: Many villagers said they had received basic first aid training in primary school.
Women in remote districts struggled to get care from distant health centres.
Most of the injured were farmers walking home from the weekly market at night.
She took a bus to the district Government Hospital in the next town for her check-up.
Young men learned carpentry at a vocational institute run by the church.
The survey found that children often missed meals at boarding schools in the hills.
Patients had to travel for hours to obtain medicine from the regional clinic.
He said he first learned to read at a night school for adults in the village.
quiet: Many villagers said they had never received any basic first aid training at all.
Women in remote districts struggled with long hours and low wages for years.
Most of the injured were farmers who had been working late into the night.
She took a bus for her check-up because her own car had broken down again.
Young men learned carpentry from their fathers and uncles over many years.
The survey found that children often missed meals during the dry season.
Patients had to wait for hours because there were too few doctors on duty.
He said he first learned to read when he was already a grown man of thirty.
